title: 0.999... equals 1. Exactly.
voiceover: Zero point nine nine nine, repeating forever, equals one. Not almost one. Not rounding. Exactly one. Don't believe it? Call it x. So x is zero point nine repeating. Multiply both sides by ten: ten x is nine point nine repeating. Now subtract the first equation from the second. On the left, ten x minus x is nine x. On the right, the infinite tails of nines cancel perfectly — leaving just nine. So nine x equals nine. Which means x equals one. Here's the part that breaks brains: they were never two different numbers sitting close together. They're the same number — written two different ways.
